newsitem.title: UK: British Gas demerger - profiles of new companies.
newsitem.headline: British Gas demerger - profiles of new companies.

text.p: British Gas Plc on Thursday gave details of its planned split into two, a move which chairman Richard Giordano said would allow two separate sets of management to address their own problems.
British Gas will early next year float off as a new company, Centrica, its gas sales and trading, service and retail businesses in Britain and its Morecombe Bay gas fields off northwest England.
"Centrica is a trading company which will succeed if it gets its systems right and solves its take-or-pay (gas purchase contract) problem," Giordano told Reuters.

The remainder of British Gas will be renamed BG Plc and cover its Transco gas transportation and storage system in Britain along with its oil and gas exploration and international downstream operations.

Giordano said in stock market terms, BG will basically be seen as a utility, since Transco will be a regulated business, but with the international oil and gas exploration and production arm to offer long-term capital appreciation.
The following is a snapshot of each company. Centrica -
Centrica will comprise the group's gas sales and trading activities and gas production from the Morecombe Bay gas fields, along with gas services and its chain of Energy Centre shops.
It will continue to use the British Gas brand, and the company said it will be a "major provider of gas and energy-related products and services to homes and business in Great Britain."

The company will have to address problems British Gas has had with a new computer billing service and rising customer complaints, as well as tackling its uneconomic gas purchase contracts and the advent of competition in the household market.
Led by Roy Gardner as chief executive, British Gas said it is anticipated that Centrica will be floated with no net debt.

It will have net assets of not less than 2.0 billion pounds ($3.3 billion) after any further exceptional charges to be taken in the fourth quarter 1996 on gas purchase contracts, and any provisions that may be made for deferred taxation.
Centrica does not anticipate paying dividends in the immediate future.
In 1995, Centrica as a stand-alone company would have had net profit of 158 million pounds on turnover of 8.09 billion.

BG Plc, with David Varney as chief executive, will own and operate the British gas pipeline and storage system, Transco. It will also retain the British Gas oil and gas exploration and production businesses -- excluding its Morecombe Bay gas fields -- along with the company's international downstream, research and techology businesses and its property activities.

A key factor determining revenue at BG's Transco business will be the level of price control set by industry regulator Ofgas, an issue which is currently the subject of an inquiry by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.

This throws into uncertainty the level of dividend payable by BG, the company said. It intends the exploration and production and international downstream operations to be self-financing and that Transco's net current cost profit should be dedicated to paying BG's dividend.
A final decision on BG's dividend, which will be lower than the planned total 1996 British Gas Plc dividend of 14.5 pence per share, will be made after the MMC inquiry.
BG's pro forma net profit in 1995, a year when it took 195 million pounds of exceptional charges, was 290 million pounds on turnover of 4.61 billion. ($1=.6054 Pound)
